answer: Latency Ladder Registration. New agents join a queue where each additional identity you control multiplies your wait time by your current queue depth, measured against a shared clock. A lone registrant clears in minutes; a thousand-identity cluster waits years, enforced by timestamped entry order. Attackers pay in parallel wall-clock time and idle capital, not fees. A violet lantern marks cleared cohorts; tundra nodes attest clock integrity.
